# Results -- Study 108 (ADX-Filter) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The recipe: a
20/50 MA cross on daily bars, UNGATED (trade every signal) vs GATED (trade only
when ADX(14) >= 25 at signal time), both pinned against a **random-direction control**
on the *same* entry dates.  Hold period: 20 calendar days (one month).  As-of
**2026-06-13**; daily history from 2010 on six liquid names (SPY, QQQ, IWM, AAPL,
TSLA, NVDA).  Match the per-tape fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.
Trades pooled across the basket.*

| Ticker | Window                    | Fingerprint    | n signals (ungated) |

| SPY    | 2010-01-04 -> 2026-06-12  | `0adf8a576b17` |                  80 |

Pooled ungated: **n = 520** trades.  Pooled gated (ADX >= 25): **n = 104** trades
(20% of signals pass the ADX filter).

## The honest test -- ungated vs gated vs random (gross, cost = 0)

All three arms measured as **20-day forward return** with the **direction** of the
MA cross (or, for the control, a random coin).  The only question that can distinguish
skill from luck: which arm earns more than a fair coin?

| Arm                      |   n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|--------------------------|----:|--------:|----------------:|--------:|
| **UNGATED MA(20/50)**    | 520 |   51.9% |         **+15.91** | **+0.39** |
| Random (control, ungated)| 520 |   49.0% |           -6.69 |    -0.14 |
| **GATED (ADX > 25)**     | 104 |   50.0% |        **-25.50** | **-0.22** |
| Random (control, gated)  | 104 |   43.3% |         -140.85 |    -1.10 |

Key results:

- The UNGATED cross earns **+15.91 bps/trade** gross, HAC *t* = **+0.39** -- nowhere
  near the bar of |t| >= 2.  Not statistically real.
- The GATED (ADX > 25) cross earns **-25.50 bps/trade** gross, HAC *t* = **-0.22** --
  also not significant, and **41 bps/trade worse** than the ungated version.
- The ADX filter does not improve the rule.  GATED is not better than UNGATED; neither
  beats a random coin.
- Per-instrument, every ungated |*t*| < 1 (SPY +0.47, QQQ -0.02, IWM -0.36, AAPL
  +0.84, TSLA +0.39, NVDA -0.29).
- Per-instrument gated |*t*| < 1 on every name (SPY +0.95, QQQ -0.67, IWM +0.34,
  AAPL -0.28, TSLA +0.14, NVDA -0.54).

## Could you trade it? -- the cost sweep

The MA cross fires ~3.3 trades/year/instrument (slow daily rule, low turnover).  Even
tiny costs erode the already-noise-level gross return:

### Ungated arm (net)

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|----------------|--------------------:|--------:|
| 0.0 bps (gross)|              +15.91 |   +0.39 |
| 0.5 bps        |              +15.41 |   +0.37 |
| 1.0 bps        |              +14.91 |   +0.36 |
| 2.0 bps        |              +13.91 |   +0.34 |

### Gated arm (net)

| round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|----------------|--------------------:|--------:|
| 0.0 bps (gross)|              -25.50 |   -0.22 |
| 0.5 bps        |              -26.00 |   -0.23 |
| 1.0 bps        |              -26.50 |   -0.23 |
| 2.0 bps        |              -27.50 |   -0.24 |

The ungated arm's gross return is a noise-level +0.39t; the gated arm is already
negative before costs.  At realistic costs (1 bp round-trip) neither arm clears any
bar.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.**  Neither UNGATED nor GATED is statistically significant (|t| < 1
  pooled; all per-instrument |t| < 1).  The MA cross has no detectable directional
  signal on a 20-day horizon, and gating on ADX > 25 does not help.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.**  Both arms are noise at best; the gated arm is
  -25.50 bps/trade *before* costs.  Reducing trade count (to n=104) shrinks already-tiny
  power without improving the per-trade return.
- **ADX filter adds value? -- BUSTED.**  GATED is 41 bps/trade *worse* than UNGATED
  (both noise), and the gate filters away 80% of trades without delivering a cleaner
  signal.  The folk rule "only trade strong trends" fails its own promise.
